newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end firm on wheat, world demand.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end firm on wheat, world demand.

text.p: CBOT soyoil and soymeal futures ended higher on Tuesday, supported by a rally in wheat futures and by USDA world demand figures, traders said.
"The market shrugged the report off, the numbers were already in the pit," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
USDA on Tuesday pegged U.S. soybean output at 2.403 billion bushels, above the average of trade expectations for 2.376 billion bushels.
But the report also showed an increase in Chinese demand for soybeans and soymeal.

China was expected to buy 1.6 million tonnes of soymeal, up from last month's projection of 1.4 million tonnes. USDA also forecast China would purchase 1.0 million tonnes of soybeans, compared with 900,000 on last month's report.
USDA lowered its projection for Argentina's soybean crop by 500,000 tonnes to 13 million tonnes which further fueled ideas demand for U.S. soybeans and products would increase.
Soyoil futures closed 0.31 to 0.24 cent per pound higher with December up 0.29 at 23.04 while soymeal closed up $4.10 to $1.30 per ton with December up $4.00 at $230.70.
The report showed soybean crushing rates at 1.390 billion bushels, up from 1.375 billion last month.
Traders noted cash basis values in the country remained strong and crush margins were high.
Soybean crushing rates were near record highs in October yet demand outpaced supply.
Cargill Inc, ADM Investor Services, Produce Grain and Term Commodities were all said to be buyers of soyoil.
Refco Inc bought at least 2,000 lots of soymeal on the day, traders said.
Soyoil volume was estimated by CBOT at 17,000 contracts, well above the 10,302 traded on Monday.
Soymeal volume was estimated at 36,000 contracts, more than twice the 15,293 contracts traded on Monday.
